concept: Combobox is Input's recessed well with a list that opens under it and narrows as you type, so a person who knows the word can write it and a person who does not can read the choices; it takes only a listed option and never leaves free text behind.
family_difference: Combobox lets the person type into the well to filter the options, shows a count and a no-match line, and drops free text on leaving, where Select only opens a list.

default_to_avoid.pattern: Combobox as an autocomplete search box with a magnifier, free text accepted and suggestions in a white card with a blue highlighted row
default_to_avoid.why_not: Free text breaks a choice that must be one of the listed options, the blue row tells the reached state by hue alone and spends a colour P1 keeps for one part, and a search glyph makes it look like a different part.

default_to_avoid.pattern: native input with a datalist element, drawn by the operating system
default_to_avoid.why_not: The system draws its own popup and type, which ignore the material and the light, cannot show a leading mark, and announce differently in every browser.

references.source: Braun T 1000 world receiver (Dieter Rams, 1963): a station name printed on the case and a dial that lets you find it by the first letters

system/FORM.md input class: recessed well, full width of its column, label printed above on the inset line; the open list reuses Select and Popover plastic (surface.solid, elevation.float, corner.inner)
WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices: combobox with list autocomplete (https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/combobox/)

derivation.consequence: the window is recessed into the body (inverse light)
derivation.form: The text well is the same recess as Input and Select: surface.sunken with elevation.well and a line.ring hairline, full width of its column.

derivation.consequence: labels sit on the body's inset line, never floating mid-surface
derivation.form: The label is printed above the well at its start edge and names the field through its for attribute; the placeholder is a separate grey prompt and never the name.

derivation.consequence: links, borders, icons, selections and charts never use it
derivation.form: The chosen option carries a printed tick and medium weight in primary ink, and the letters that match the typed text turn medium; no row is ever filled orange or blue.
The open list is surface.solid plastic with elevation.float and corner.inner on layer.overlay, the same panel as Select and Popover, and nothing deeper.

derivation.consequence: every mechanism has its keyboard map
derivation.form: Focus stays in the well; the arrows reach rows through aria-activedescendant, Page keys jump ten, Enter chooses, Escape closes and restores the text, and Alt with Down opens.

derivation.consequence: no entry choreography, no idle animation; transitions only on state
derivation.form: The list rises out of the well when it opens and sinks back faster when it closes, a row inks in when it is reached, and nothing moves while the list sits open (D-008).

options.name: Input well, Select's plastic panel floating under it, matched letters in medium weight
one recess that grows downward from the well, options inside the same window
printed legend under the well with no container, ink index bar at the reached word

variants.reason: A floats on layer.overlay so it covers the fields below without moving them and its edge says it is a separate layer (P6 depth); B has no shadow, so over the next field it reads as part of the page, and C has no edge, so it either pushes the form down or sits on the next label.

root.why: The field stacks its label, well and messages in one column and is the anchor the open list hangs from, so the list lines up with the well.

label.why: The printed name uses the label size in medium weight, like the printing beside every other part of the unit.

anchor.why: The well and the open list share one box that the list hangs from, so the list lines up with the well and does not shift when a hint or error is printed under it.

well.why: The recess takes the inverse light, shade on its top-left inner edge, so the person sees where the typed words go.

mark.why: The leading mark of the chosen option, such as an avatar, stands at the start of the well on the same inset line as the marks in the rows.

field.why: Typed text is primary ink on the sunken plastic at more than 4.5:1, with a line box tall enough for stacked Thai marks.

toggle.why: A 44px key at the end of the well opens and closes the list for a finger, and stays out of the tab order because the field already has the keyboard.

chevron.why: A printed chevron in secondary ink says a list is behind the well, and it turns over while the list is open.

panel.why: The list is plastic above the page with the float shadow, at least as wide as the well, so it reads as a separate layer and not as part of the form.

option.why: Every row is at least 44px tall so a finger can pick it, with its text inset from the rounded ends.

tick.why: A printed tick in ink marks the chosen row, so a choice never uses the orange or a tinted fill; an empty tick keeps the column so words do not shift.

leading.why: An optional mark such as an icon or an avatar stands between the tick and the words, so rows with and without one still align.

text.why: Option words use the body size of the one grotesk, with a line box tall enough for stacked Thai marks, and long words wrap instead of being cut.

match.why: The letters that match what was typed turn medium weight in primary ink, a cue that survives a black and white screen and never needs a highlight colour.

empty.why: When nothing matches, one plain line in secondary ink sits in the list, so the person learns the typed text has no option and the list does not close.

hint.why: The hint is secondary ink in the caption size under the well.

error.why: The error is critical red with a glyph and words, never orange and never colour alone.

glyph.why: A printed mark beside the words means invalid is never told by colour alone, for people who cannot see the red.

md.why: The default well and rows are 44px tall, the smallest target that every part in dial keeps for a finger.

lg.why: A 52px well and rows with larger text for the main choice of a phone sheet held in one hand.

focus-within.why: The well shows the same dark ring as every part when its field holds the keyboard focus, and the reached row inside the list carries its own plate.

data-invalid=true.why: An invalid well draws its edge in the critical red, which is never orange, and the message below names the problem.

data-disabled=true.why: A disabled field loses its recess shadow and fades to half, so it reads as not taking input right now.

aria-expanded=true.why: While the list is open the chevron turns over, a cue of shape that works without colour.

aria-selected=true.why: The chosen row is primary ink in medium weight with its tick, never a coloured fill behind the words.

aria-disabled=true.why: A row that cannot be chosen fades to half and the arrows skip it, so it stays readable but is plainly not part of the walk.

data-active=true.why: The row under the keyboard or the pointer sinks into a well, so the reached row is shown by depth and an edge, not hue.

data-state=open.why: The list is mounted in the same render that opens it, so the input and aria-controls always point at a list that exists.

data-state=closing.why: A leaving list is inert and hidden from assistive tech, because it is only a picture of the list while it fades out.

data-on=true.why: The tick of the chosen row fades in over motion.hover, so the choice is told by a printed mark that appears and not by a fill.

@media forced-colors: active.why: In forced colours the well keeps a real border, the list gets a border, and the focus ring and the reached row use the system highlight colour.

@media prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.why: Under Reduce motion nothing travels (motion.rise is 0) and the list still fades on motion.hover, which the tokens keep (D-008).

transform.why: Opening is a state change, so it moves. The list rises a step (motion.rise) over motion.release on the decelerating curve, the chevron turns with it, and the list leaves over motion.exit on the accelerating one (D-008). Under Reduce motion only the fade stays.

opacity.why: The list fades in over motion.release and out over motion.exit, and the tick of the chosen row fades with the choice on motion.hover, so a change is seen arriving (D-008).

background-color.why: The reached row sinks into a well and inks in on motion.hover, fast on and slower off, so the arrows read as walking down the list instead of jumping.

box-shadow.why: The reached row sinks into a well and inks in on motion.hover, fast on and slower off, so the arrows read as walking down the list instead of jumping.

color.why: The reached row sinks into a well and inks in on motion.hover, fast on and slower off, so the arrows read as walking down the list instead of jumping.
